purpose: The VMLU Test column of the /table before-and-after table for MiMo: MiMo's within-run direct answer (before, B-r1) and MC-105's self-improvement loop (after) on the 9,833 VMLU test items, whose gold only vmlu.ai holds. Each attempt is asked only when the loop's rule needs it, so the final answer is the one MC-105's offline replay would choose from the same attempts. MC-109 did the same for Qwen.

items.source: the frozen vi-multimodel v2 VMLU manifest data/vi_multimodel_v2/vmlu_v2.json, test split, the items and prompts of the /table VMLU Test runs (MC-83 direct)
items.gold: withheld: only vmlu.ai scores the test split

arm_meaning.B: the frozen v2 VMLU prompt, byte for byte the /table VMLU Test prompt, asked twice (B-r1, B-r2) as in MC-105
arm_meaning.S: the campaign step-by-step template of data/diagnostic_prospective_v1/prompt_templates_v1.json, as in MC-90 to MC-105 and MC-109

schedule.rule: round by round: B-r1 and B-r2 for every item; S-r1 only when B-r1 and B-r2 do not agree; S-r2 and S-r3 only when S-r1 agrees with neither
schedule.passes: each pass sends every attempt the rule needs from the completed attempts so far; an attempt without a completed response (a technical failure, not a fatal one) is sent again in the next pass; a launch stops after max_passes passes, after a pass that completes nothing, or at any fatal row
schedule.equivalence: the attempts are independent requests, so the final answer equals the one diagnostic_table_loop.choose (MC-105's replay) returns on the same attempts; the attempts the rule never needs are not sent

mimo.route: MC-105's MiMo route (the MC-103 request): OpenCode Go chat completions, no streaming, system prompt Answer the user's question., 20,000 completion tokens, 300 s timeout, no SDK retries, one x-opencode-session per attempt; the same request for B and S
mimo.max_in_flight_source: MC-105's registered value for MiMo, the owner's choice on 2026-11-07
mimo.budget_source: projected from MC-105's MiMo VMLU valid rounds and usage: about 7.7 million for the two B answers and 2 to 4 million for S; 20,000,000 as for MC-109

loop.agreement: router v2's normalized-answer-v1 (diagnostic_router.answers_agree): both parsed letters non-empty and equal
loop.rule: MC-104 and MC-105 for MiMo's multiple choice: round 1 keeps B-r1 when B-r1 and B-r2 agree; round 2 keeps S-r1 when it agrees with one of them; round 3 takes the majority of S-r1 to S-r3 (a tie to the earliest; an empty answer casts no vote; with no answer S-r1 is final)
loop.final_answer: always one of the student's own logged answers

table_conditions.mimo: MC-85 (direct API, 77.68 on vmlu.ai), MC-63 (OMP without tools, 76.20) and MC-89 (OMP full tools, 79.60), as /table shows them

reference.valid_rounds: MC-105 on VMLU valid, MiMo: round 1 611, round 2 115, round 3 17 of the 743 items with both B answers
reference.qwen_test: MC-109: Qwen's loop on the same items, 67.09 before and 76.63 after on vmlu.ai

analysis.outputs: the runner writes loop.jsonl (per item: the attempts the rule read, their letters, the rounds and the final answer), summary.json, and, once every item has a final answer, submission_before.csv (B-r1) and submission_loop.csv (the loop), both id,answer for vmlu.ai
analysis.scores: accuracy on vmlu.ai for the two submissions, entered from vmlu.ai's reply; the owner submits them
analysis.primary: the loop's accuracy minus the before's accuracy on vmlu.ai, descriptive: with item-level gold withheld there is no paired test
descriptive: the rounds the loop used, beside MC-105's MiMo VMLU valid rounds
how many final answers differ from B-r1, and how often B-r1 and B-r2 disagree
mean reported tokens per item, both B answers included, and latency
the /table VMLU Test numbers of MC-85, MC-63 and MC-89 beside the two scores, and MC-109's Qwen scores
